extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys, and agents seeking to correct inventorship or inventor names/order in a U.S. patent application
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and checklist for filing a Request under 37 CFR 1.48 (PTO/AIA/40) to correct inventorship, inventor names, or the order of names in a U.S. patent application (nonreissue and provisional). Covers required documents, fees, signatures, and timing restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of PTO/AIA/40 (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for correction in a patent application relating to inventorship or an inventor name, or order of names, other than in a reissue application (37 CFR 1.48).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: 37 CFR 1.48 applies to any request to correct inventorship filed on or after September 16, 2012, regardless of the application filing date. Do not submit this form after payment of the issue fee or if the application has been patented. See 37 CFR 1.324 for correction of inventorship in a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional application — ADS showing corrected inventorship (1.48(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a nonprovisional application requesting correction or change of inventorship, include an application data sheet (ADS) in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76(c) with the corrected or updated information shown with markings (e.g., underlining for insertions, strikethrough for deletions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 601.05(a) for information about filing an ADS in an application filed on/after September 16, 2012. For a Supplemental ADS in an application filed before September 16, 2012, see MPEP 601.05(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fee for nonprovisional corrections (37 CFR 1.17(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i) is required for correction requests in a nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form provides a space to indicate amount; additional fee rules (see separate entry) may apply if filed after the first Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding an inventor — inventor's oath/declaration required (1.48(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is being added, an inventor's oath or declaration by any actual inventor who has not yet executed an oath or declaration is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 602.01(a) for information about an inventor's oath or declaration for an application filed on/after September 16, 2012 (e.g., form PTO/AIA/01). For applications filed before September 16, 2012, see MPEP 602.01(b) (e.g., form PTO/SB/01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-first-action filings — cancellation vs. additional fee (1.48(c) and 1.17(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request is filed after the first Office action on the merits has been given or mailed, indicate whether the request to correct inventorship is due solely to the cancellation of claims in the application or whether the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(d) is due (in addition to 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form instructs filer to check one of the two options and to pay the additional fee if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional application — change/update inventor name or order (1.48(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For changing or updating the name of an inventor or a joint inventor, or the order of names of joint inventors, include an ADS per 37 CFR 1.76(c) identifying the complete inventive entity and showing corrections/updates with markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 601.05(a) for ADS filing rules for applications filed on/after September 16, 2012; see MPEP 601.05(b) for Supplemental ADS guidance for earlier filings. Processing fee per 37 CFR 1.17(i) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application — signed document identifying inventors (1.48(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a provisional application, the request must be accompanied by a document signed by a party set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(b) that identifies each inventor by his or her legal name in the preferred order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document may be an ADS in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76(c) that identifies the changes with markings (underlining for insertions, strikethrough for deletions). The processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(q) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark corrections clearly on ADS (underlining/strikethrough)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections or updated information on an ADS should be shown with markings (e.g., underlining for insertions, strikethrough for deletions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This marking convention is referenced for both applications filed on/after and before September 16, 2012, with MPEP 601.05(a)/(b) providing filing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment methods and entity-status certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide payment for required fees and assert small or micro entity status if applicable (see 37 CFR 1.27 and 1.29). Include Form PTO/SB/15A or B or equivalent if claiming small/micro entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment options: check, credit card (use PTO-2038 for credit card info), authorize Director to charge/credit a deposit account, provide Deposit Account No., or pay via USPTO patent electronic filing system. WARNING: Information on this form may become public; credit card information should not be included on this form—use PTO-2038.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, signature requirements, and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The form must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33; see 37 CFR 1.4 for signature requirements and certifications. Juristic entities must be represented by a patent practitioner (see 37 CFR 1.31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide typed/printed name and date; include registration number for attorney/agent of record. Submit multiple forms if more than one signature is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act notice and consequence of noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Act statement explains the USPTO's authority to collect information and routine uses of collected data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requested information is not furnished, the USPTO may not be able to process and/or examine the submission, which may result in termination of proceedings, abandonment of the application, and/or expiration of the patent. The form includes routine uses and possible disclosures (law enforcement, other agencies, courts, FOIA considerations, contractors, congressional inquiries, etc.).
